title: Book Three · Chapter 105: The Proposal in the Letter
story:
On Tuesday, Ronan finishes his sixteenth letter to Leo.

He starts with Mrs Deng's return. Then he copies the cash and book counts from the account sheet.

We have forty-one yuan. Ten books are good. Two have missing pages. Both cloth bags are still here.

He reads the lines once. They tell Leo the result, but they do not decide the next step.

Ronan writes a proposal below them.

I want to finish the shared sale. We could each keep five good books and one bag. We could split the cash equally. Mr Qiu can use old pages to wrap pencils. I can ask him about the damaged books and the old large card.

He stops and reads the proposal aloud. Mum looks up from her sewing.

“Are you asking me?”

“No. Sorry.”

“Then leave Leo room to answer.”

Ronan looks at his next line. He has begun to write that he will take the bag tomorrow. He crosses that line out. Tomorrow is too soon for a reply.

He turns the sheet a little. There is still space for Leo to choose different books. Ronan looks at the shelf once more, then returns to the letter.

He leaves a space, then writes about Leo's share.

Would you like your railway book and garden book, with three B books? Grandmother may keep your bag and money for you. I will ask her too.

Ronan puts down the pen. None of the books has changed owner yet. He has only written the idea.

He signs the letter, folds it, and puts it in an envelope. At the post office, he pays for the stamp from his own spending money. He posts the letter there. The shared forty-one stays at home.

After school the next day, Kai waits near the gate.

“Now?” he asks, with the football under his arm.

Ronan looks at the white mark. It is his own ball, ready for a game.

“Half an hour.”

“I can lose in that time.”

“Try not to.”

They go to the grass with two other boys. For the first few minutes, Ronan is slow. He is thinking about envelopes and the next reply.

Then a pass comes low toward his foot. He stops it, turns, and sends it across to Kai.

“There you are,” Kai says.

Ronan laughs. He runs after the next ball.

At the bell from a nearby building, the boys stop. Kai needs to go home. Ronan collects his ball and walks with him to the corner.

“Still selling?” Kai asks.

“No. Waiting for Leo's answer about the end.”

“Does waiting need both feet?”

Ronan looks down at his shoes and smiles.

“Apparently not.”

At home, he puts the football beside the bike. He checks his homework, then returns the shared envelope to its place.

He will need Leo's answer before any split. Tonight, the ten good books remain together on the shelf. Ronan takes out his school work and leaves the cash sheet closed beside them.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

proposal＝提议；share＝应分得的一份；equally＝平均地；wrap＝包裹。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan提出怎样分钱、分完整书和袋子？这时是否已经执行？
2. 他买邮票的钱从哪里出？共同现金有没有因此改变？

## 读句子

**The shared forty-one stays at home.**

拆开看：The shared forty-one / stays / at home.

共同的四十一元／仍留着／留在家里。
